neighbours.label: the possessive pronoun right after 'shook' (shook his / her / my head or fist), as against the same possessive after other head-movement verbs
fire: The farmer looked at the dry field and shook his head in despair.
When the nurse offered more soup, the patient shook her head politely.
After reading the letter twice, I shook my head and put it away.
The captain heard the forecast and shook his head at the crew.
Asked if she was tired, the little girl shook her head stubbornly.
The angry neighbour leaned over the fence and shook his fist at us.
Our teacher read the excuse aloud and shook her head with a smile.
Hearing the price, my father frowned and shook his head firmly.
quiet: The farmer looked at the dry field and lowered his head in despair.
When the nurse offered more soup, the patient turned her head away.
After reading the letter twice, I rubbed my eyes and put it away.
The captain heard the forecast and nodded his head at the crew.
Asked if she was tired, the little girl rested her head on the pillow.
The angry neighbour leaned over the fence and shook the gate hard.
Our teacher read the excuse aloud and tilted her head with a smile.
Hearing the price, my father frowned and raised his eyebrows.
